import re

# Proposed new regex with correct numeric handling
new_regex = re.compile(
    r'''
    ^
    (?P<major>(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*))
    \.
    (?P<minor>(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*))
    \.
    (?P<patch>(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*))
    (\-(?P<prerelease>
        (?:[0-9]*[1-9][0-9]*|[0-9A-Za-z-]+(?:\.[0-9A-Za-z-]+)*)
    ))?
    (\+(?P<build>
        [0-9A-Za-z-]+(\.[0-9A-Za-z-]+)*
    ))?
    $
    ''', re.VERBOSE)

test_versions = [
    '1.0.0',           # valid
    '0.0.0',           # valid
    '01.0.0',          # invalid - leading zero
    '1.01.0',          # invalid - leading zero
    '1.0.0-alpha',     # valid
    '1.0.0-',          # invalid - trailing hyphen
    '-1.0.0',          # invalid
    '1.0.0+build',     # valid
    '1.0.0+',          # invalid
    '1.0.0-0',         # valid - numeric prerelease
    '1.0.0-00',        # invalid - leading zero in prerelease
    '1.0.0-alpha.0',   # valid
    '1.0.0-alpha.-',   # check this
    '1.0.0-alpha.',    # invalid - trailing dot
    '.1.0.0',          # invalid
    '1.0.0..alpha',    # invalid - double dot
    '',                # invalid
    '1.0',             # invalid - missing patch
    '1.0.0.0',         # invalid - extra component
    '1.2.3-alpha.1.2+build.11.e0f985a',  # from tests
    '1.2.3-alpha-1+build.11.e0f985a',    # from tests
    '1.0.0-rc.1',      # valid
    '1.0.0+2013.12.24', # valid - build with dots
    '1.0.0-0.3.7',     # valid - mix of numeric and alpha prerelease
    '1.0.0-x.7.z.92',  # valid - from spec
    '1.0.0-alpha+001', # valid - from spec
    '1.0.0+21AF26D3',  # valid - from spec
    '1.0.0-0A',        # valid - from spec
]

for v in test_versions:
    match = new_regex.match(v)
    status = 'VALID' if match else 'INVALID'
    print(f'{v:45} -> {status}')"

raw_message.reasoning:
Hmm, `1.0.0-00` is now VALID with my proposed regex. But according to semver.org, numeric identifiers must not have leading zeros. The spec says:

"Numeric identifiers MUST NOT include leading zeroes."

So `00` should be INVALID. My regex `(?:[0-9]+|[0-9A-Za-z-]+(?:\.[0-9A-Za-z-]+)*)` would match `00` as a pure numeric identifier `[0-9]+`, but it should only match numbers without leading zeros.

I need to use the official pattern for numeric identifiers: `[0-9]*[1-9][0-9]*`.
